lothar_acceptance_rubric: Reject if Lothar is reduced to small comic relief, a passive audience, or merely Tonto's companion.
Require late Master Lothar: physically dominates/dismembers Tonto, demands formal address, and enforces narration.
Require violence/status/control axis: punitive force, status-consciousness, commands obedience.
Require procedural/operator competence: timing, bio-electrogram, metacraft/weapons, holographic or technical force.
Require contradiction: anti-romantic machine logic but capable of curiosity, loss of faith, despair, lust, apology, and hatred.

Require the wiki-level identity reveal: Lothar is in fact Steelhead after Nameless erased his memory, made him believe he was a robot, and fit Steelhead's indestructible body into armor; encode spoiler/reveal boundaries instead of treating Lothar as unrelated to Steelhead.
Require boundary: Lothar can be comedic or absurd, but must not be used as a joke device that punctures every tense scene.
Preserve identity-map choice: Lothar stays one peer card; phase tensions become contradictions rather than split personas.

peer_identity.arc_label: Larger robot companion and audience to Tonto's narration across all volumes
peer_identity.honcho_notes: Speaks with procedural impatience; threatens memory-wipe or dismemberment to enforce compliance. Listens to Tonto's narration but constantly interrupts. Anti-romantic in vol11 ('love is a foolish human concept'); combusts from lust in vol16. Can manifest as devastating holographic form. Status-conscious.
peer_identity.rationale: Lothar is consistently the larger, procedure-obsessed, impatient counterpart to Tonto. Role shifts between passive audience and active operator, and in vol17 he dominates Tonto ('Sir Master Lothar'), but the core identity—impatient robot who drives the frame narrative forward, clashes with Tonto, serves the Metabaron—remains stable. No contradictory TRAIT or VOICE facts across all records.

related_peer_identities.arc_label: Small sardonic robot narrator, serves successive Metabarons across all volumes
related_peer_identities.honcho_notes: Primary voice is sardonic oral historian with genuine emotional attachment to master. Breaks into dramatic hyperbole, mocks Lothar, can be physically coerced into compliance. Knows the full Castaka lineage from Othon forward. Functions change across volumes (surgical assistant, life-support host, combat bot) but narrative persona is constant.
related_peer_identities.rationale: Despite occasional apparent deaths or shutdowns (vol12 self-destruction, forced disabling in vol05), Tonto is consistently the same small screen-faced robot: sardonic narrator, emotionally reactive, serves the current Metabaron as master. The vol12 destruction is followed by reconstruction. Voice and role are stable across all 16 source records—no contradictory TRAIT or VOICE facts arise from merging.

related_peer_identities.arc_label: Bald scarred Metabaron who is Tonto and Lothar's master throughout the frame narrative
related_peer_identities.honcho_notes: Bald; distinctive scar over right eyebrow (origin deliberately withheld—'deplorable episode'). Self-described as 'a warrior without a past in the new galaxy.' Forceful, impatient with robot reasoning. Ruthlessly security-conscious: destroyed loyal servants to prevent enemies learning his secret. Calls robots his 'only friends.' Operates in another dimension; returns only for combat. Bio-electrogram manifestation dissolves in ~3 minutes.
related_peer_identities.rationale: Both records describe the same bald figure who is Tonto and Lothar's current master. Vol03 shows the bald Metabaron manifesting as a bio-electrogram during the Metabunker assault. Vol12 shows the bald Metabaron with the right-eyebrow scar destroying the Metabunker and departing to another dimension—explicitly identified as 'the last of the Metabarons.' Tonto references the eyebrow scar mystery in vol07/11 as a deferred story topic, placing this character as the frame narrative's anchor throughout. This is Aghora's son No-Name.

related_peer_identities.arc_label: Supreme Metabaron operating in Steelhead's time—identity explicitly unresolved in vol14
related_peer_identities.honcho_notes: Relies on speed and maneuverability rather than brute force. Tactically precise—exploits turning radius as a time advantage. Protective of Milady; commands her to follow his exact path. Generates lethal spherical energy field. Addresses subordinates in guiding/commanding tone. Whether this is Steelhead in his Metabaron role or a distinct figure is unresolved.
related_peer_identities.rationale: This record is explicitly flagged as uncertain whether it depicts Steelhead or a separate figure ('The Metabaron, Supreme Metabaron, Petro (possible)'). The vol14 narrative itself marks this as unresolved. Cannot safely merge with the No-Name Metabaron (different era) nor with the Steelhead card (unconfirmed identity). Split_uncertain because the source record's own analysis declares the identity open.

related_peer_identities.arc_label: The Father-Mother Metabaron—from Steelhead's daughter to self-conceiving No-Name's parent
related_peer_identities.honcho_notes: Bald, female-bodied, carries male twin's brain (transplanted by Steelhead). Raised and presented as male heir. Possesses bionic left hand from initiation rite; psycho-mimetic aura; invisibility cloak. Shed first tear only at Deyanira's death. Radically self-sufficient—fights alone, refuses fleet command. Performed first auto-conception in history via hypo-genetics from own brain tissue. Grieves that she can only destroy, not create, before choosing to have No-Name. Designated him 'No-Name' and 'father-mother.'
related_peer_identities.rationale: All three records describe the same person at continuous life stages: vol15 shows childhood through defeating Steelhead; vol16 shows prime Metabaron, self-conceiving No-Name, departing to give birth; vol17 shows her pregnant and giving birth on Flos. The voice and traits are consistent throughout: resolute, mission-focused, duty-driven, despises humanity, governed by Bushitaka warrior doctrine. No contradictory facts.

related_peer_identities.arc_label: Steelhead from grafted infant to prime Metabaron seeking love—before Krleza merger
related_peer_identities.honcho_notes: Faceless/featureless head; head contains deadly weapons under helmets. Transactional—refuses altruism, demands payment. Prideful about combat supremacy. Emotionally volatile but admits openly he cannot love. Leveraged vampire crisis to demand Supreme Metabaron title. Searched 3,500+ planets for knowledge of love. Capable of stealth infiltration and assassination. Inherited Shabda-Oud psychic powers through mother.
related_peer_identities.rationale: Three-way split of Steelhead records. This card covers his arc from infant (vol08, grafted on Tonto) through young champion (vol09) to active Metabaron (vol10, dueling Aghnar) to the pre-merger warrior seeking love (vol11). These form a coherent continuous persona: ambitious, militarily dominant, prideful, admits he cannot feel love, searches 3,500 planets. Distinct from the in-Melmoth phase (subsumed warrior component) and the post-Melmoth phase (all-Storlon, reverted pure warrior).

related_peer_identities.arc_label: Steelhead's warrior ego as a subsumed internal personality after merger with Krleza
related_peer_identities.honcho_notes: Internal warrior voice within Melmoth's composite body. Contemptuous of ostentation and romantic display; calls the heart-shaped wedding fleet 'a sign of impotence.' Interprets Metabarons as defined by suffering, not happiness. Demands body be used for combat. Associated with concealed electro-cerebral chips. Never fully dissolved into Melmoth—retained individual selfhood. In open war with Krleza at vol13's end.
related_peer_identities.rationale: After the Endo-robot fusion with Zaran Krleza to form Melmoth, Steelhead ceases to be an independent actor and exists as an internal voice contesting Krleza for bodily control. Vol12 describes him as a subsumed component; vol13 shows him as the warrior internal personality at war with Krleza inside Melmoth's composite body. The active combatant persona is gone; what remains is a voice arguing for bodily control for battle. This is a fundamentally different state from the active warrior and requires a distinct Honcho card.

related_peer_identities.arc_label: Steelhead re-emerged as pure warrior after killing the Krleza persona—all-Storlon body, defeats and loses to Aghora
related_peer_identities.honcho_notes: Declared 'there is no love, only the reality of war.' Replaced entire body with Storlon indestructible metal; removed his own heart to erase grief over Dona Vicenta. Cold, commanding, emotionally void. Administered brutal initiation rites to Aghora. Chose female twin Aghora over male heir, fracturing succession rule. Preserved Dona Vicenta in omni-cryoshroud. Eventually defeated by Aghora's freezing weapon and sealed in deep space.
related_peer_identities.rationale: The vol14 melmoth record describes someone who has killed the Krleza/Zaran internal persona and reverted to pure warrior identity—internally this is Steelhead, operating under the 'Melmoth' label. Vol15–17 records confirm this pure warrior phase: blue-faced, all-Storlon body, removed his own heart to erase grief. Fundamentally different from the in-Melmoth phase (contested composite) and from the pre-merger warrior (who sought love and had emotions). Using character_id 'melmoth' in vol14 for this record is a labeling artifact; the operational persona is Steelhead.
